title: Throughput assurance clause: measurable objectives, credit calculation, and customer notification windows
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Define a concise, auditable contractual clause and supporting operational playbook that: 1) states measurable throughput objectives for Dedicated customers (per-pool RPS and token/sec baselines), 2) defines how latency/throughput violations are detected and aggregated, 3) specifies error budget consumption and credit calculations, and 4) codifies customer notification and remediation windows. This ticket bundles language options for legal, measurable metric definitions for SRE/observability, and compatible billing adjustments for Finance.
background: Enterprise customers buying Dedicated capacity are asking for clearer, automatable guarantees that are both measurable and implementable without exposing operator risk. Existing docs focus on generic guarantees and error budgets, but customers want explicit detection windows, minimum sample sizes, and deterministic credit formulas. Engineering needs language that ties directly to metrics emitted by the Console (per-route throughput, pool-level capacity, backlog time) and to the error budget scheduler used by SRE.
proposal_summary: Produce a stand-alone SLA clause with three alternative remediation tiers (soft credit, pro-rated billing credit, and capacity remediation), a canonical metric set (sustained throughput, 99th percentile tail latency under target load, dropped requests due to throttling), an error-budget accounting method (rolling-window burn with minimum data window), and explicit notification/mitigation windows (T0 incident detection, T+1h customer notice, T+24h remediation plan). Deliverables: draft contract clauses for Legal, an operational runbook (SRE), sample billing credit spreadsheet (Finance), and Console dashboard template.
metrics_definition: Throughput objective: pool-level sustained tokens_per_sec measured as an exponential weighted moving average over a 5-minute window; Objective threshold X tokens/sec per committed GPU equivalent. Violation definition: sustained 5-minute window below 95% of committed throughput for at least 3 consecutive windows (>=15 minutes). Latency objective: p99 response time under committed tail_target_ms when offering low-latency routing mode. Minimum sample size: at least 1,000 requests within the rolling 15-minute window to validate an outage; if below sample size, mark as 'insufficient data' and do not charge credits unless correlated with capacity events. Detectability sources: route-level telemetry, pool-level scheduler metrics, and KV cache hit/miss rates.
credit_calculation_example: Credit basis: pro-rated daily credit computed as (CommittedThroughput - ObservedEffectiveThroughput)/CommittedThroughput * MonthlyReservedFee * A. Example: Committed 10M tokens/day, Observed 8M tokens/day across the billing window => shortfall 20%. MonthlyReservedFee = $10,000. Daily pro-rated credit = 0.2 * (10000 / 30) = $66.67. Application of caps: max credit per incident = 15% of monthly fee; cumulative credits in a billing month capped at 50% of monthly fee. Soft-credit option: if shortfall <5% for a single incident, issue a service credit token (non-monetary) instead of money back. All formulas and caps are configurable per-customer and must be surfaced in the contract appendices.
remediation_flow: 1) Detection: automated alert triggered by SRE playbook from Console anomaly detector. 2) Triage: determine if cause is customer-induced (traffic patterns, misconfiguration) vs. Redwood capacity (scheduling, kernel failure). 3) Customer notice: T+1 hour public incident email + dedicated Slack channel if enterprise plan. 4) Temporary remediation: apply burst capacity or route failover within T+4 hours if available. 5) Root-cause and credit calculation: within T+72 hours produce post-incident report and calculated credit. 6) Credit issuance: applied on next billing cycle unless customer requests immediate adjustment. 7) Follow-up: if incident recurs >2x in 30 days, escalate to account exec and legal for contract review.
acceptance_criteria: Legal approves at least two draft clause variants (monetary credit focused and remediation-focused)
SRE merges runbook into ops repo with automated alerting playbook referencing metrics defined above
Finance validates credit calculation spreadsheet and confirms billing integration feasibility
Console team creates a dashboard template and restores sample data for a partner customer
Stakeholders (Sales, Support, CS) sign off on customer-facing wording and notification windows
open_questions: Should minimum sample size be lowered for low-traffic customers or handled via soft-credits?
Do we offer a fixed SLA consumption window (calendar month) or rolling 30-day accounting?
What are acceptable caps for pro-rated credits from Legal and Finance (proposal currently uses 50% monthly cap)?
How will Dedicated burst credits interact with Reserved capacity autoscaling policies?
